newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar seen vulnerable against mark.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar seen vulnerable against mark.

text.p: The dollar slipped below psychological support at 1.50 marks on Wednesday and technical analysts said failure to get back above the figure by the close would send an ominous bearish signal.
The greenback wrestled with support near 1.4960 marks throughout the session, but even a successful defense there would not likely prevent a dip toward 1.4880, chartists said.

"Dollar/mark looks a bit weak today. We've had a sequence of lower highs and lower lows that started last week. With the descending trendline, the bias is bearish," said Martin Autotte, technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy in Montreal.
Technical analysts noted apparent head-and-shoulders patterns forming on dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss charts, with the dollar testing the neckline on each.
"The dollar/Swiss picture is not as bearish, but it is testing support at 1.2650 from last week. After that, there's really nice trendline support at 1.2530," Autotte said.
Dollar/yen looks less vulnerable, with heavy congestion on either side of 111.50 causing sustained consolidation.
But eventually dollar/yen should also continue its recent downward trend, with medium-term support seen at 110.90 or so, chartists said.
"Dollar/yen really has no direction. But the downtrend will probably resume after a little sideways consolidation," said Joseph Klettner, foreign exchange technician at Chase Securities Inc.
After initially appearing to peak in overnight trade, the sterling juggernaut continued Wednesday, with $1.68 breached again in late U.S. trade.
But chartists said cable should pull back sometime soon, with a correction long overdue after the recent stunning rise.
"We're seeing here the fifth wave of the advance from the May lows. We should see a fairly sizable correction on the downside that could eventually take us back to a $1.62 handle," Klettner said.
Mark/yen looks exuberant again, buoyed by the Monday dip to 73.50. After pushing through resistance at 74.40 on Wednesday, the cross seems poised to test higher, with initial resistance at 74.60.
"As long as it stays above 73.75 support, the mark/yen picture remains bullish," Autotte said.
